hook: "If you don't run ads below or at break-even ROAS you're probably not scaling." — contrarian scaling rule.
body: Scaling from $200–300K to $1M+ requires long-form ads that educate unaware people into the funnel; judge them on soft metrics (watch time, CTR), not ROAS; accept near-break-even on the front end (post truncated).
idea: Long-form is a scaling tool, not a conversion tool — you buy education (watch time, CTR) at break-even to widen the funnel for everything downstream.
sequencing: The rule (break-even ROAS or not scaling)
The vehicle (long-form ads educating the unaware)
The metrics (watch time, CTR — soft, not ROAS)
why_it_works: Reframes break-even spend as an investment in education rather than a failure — it gives media buyers permission to run the long-form assets that actually scale accounts.
what_to_steal: LC's long-form test KPI: judge first runs on watch time + CTR, not ROAS — the education compounds into retargeting pools.

hook: "If you haven't tested these ad formats yet, you should:" — checklist promise.
body: Five formats: (1) founder talking head — raw, 30s genuine beats polished; (2) voiceless B-roll — text-overlay bullets, clean/fast/scalable; (3) yapper — uncut organic talk, trust like a friend; (4) AI educational — AI visuals explaining mechanism, great for health; (5) camouflage ads — native-looking image + long-form ad text, emotional storytelling problem → solution → action, "people don't realize it's an ad until they're invested." Closer: format gets attention, message gets conversion — match message to persona + awareness stage.
idea: The long-form text sales letter hides inside a camouflage ad — a native-looking image carries long emotional copy (problem → solution → action) so the reader is invested before realizing it's an ad.
formatting: Text post + photo; numbered list with sub-bullets; 34 bookmarks.
why_it_works: "People don't realize it's an ad until they're invested" names the camouflage mechanism precisely — the long copy does its persuasion inside a native disguise, so defenses stay down.
what_to_steal: LC's camouflage static: an organic-looking jewelry flat-lay or wrist shot carrying long emotional copy (tarnish frustration → waterproof mechanism → stack offer) in the primary text.

product: commentary — no product (a VSL SOP promo)
hook: "97 days active. VSL's are still printing in 2026. Super scalable too. We've had VSL's that spent millions of dollars profitably." — survival proof + scale claim.
body: Promotes a detailed SOP on researching, writing, and making VSLs (Notion link): "The VSL Machine 2026 Edition — Video Sales Letters That Print."
idea: VSLs are proven by survival (97 days active) and scale (millions spent profitably) — the format's credibility comes from spend endurance, and the SOP productizes the craft.
formatting: Short text post; 83 likes, 152 bookmarks — the SOP is the product.
why_it_works: "97 days active" + "millions profitably" are the two numbers that matter for VSL credibility — endurance proves it converts, scale proves it compounds.
what_to_steal: The endurance metric for LC's long-form tests: a VSL-style ad earns "proven" status at 30+ days of profitable spend, not at launch CTR.

product: commentary — no product (a VSL swipe-file promo)
hook: "100%. VSL's print and IF you crack them, it's most scalable ad format BY FAR." — emphatic agreement + scale claim.
body: Offers 300 "banger" VSLs with 30+ day runtimes via a GetHookd board link; opens with a fake gate ("Just follow, retweet, comment ECOM UNC") then immediately undercuts it ("Joking, enjoy and print mfers").
idea: VSLs are "the most scalable ad format BY FAR" once cracked — and a 300-ad, 30+ day survival-filtered swipe file is the fastest way to study what "cracked" looks like.
sequencing: The emphatic claim (most scalable by far)
why_it_works: The fake-gate joke disarms the usual lead-magnet fatigue — giving away the 300-ad board freely makes the poster look generous while the board itself does the authority-building.
what_to_steal: The 30+ day runtime filter as LC's VSL swipe-file criterion — study only VSLs that survived a month of spend.

hook: "Don't overcomplicate testing offers, especially in the beginning." — simplification promise.
body: Claims his biggest affiliates on Meta do hundreds to 1,000+ orders/day running just 1–3 long-form ad copy variations — usually a personal story from an avatar page — "paired with dozens of" (post truncated).
idea: Long-form ad copy scales on simplicity: 1–3 personal-story variations from an avatar page can do 1,000+ orders/day — volume of variations is not the lever.
sequencing: The vehicle (1–3 long-form copy variations, personal story, avatar page)
why_it_works: "1–3 variations" counters the industry's more-is-better testing dogma — it reframes long-form as a depth game (one great story) rather than a volume game.
what_to_steal: LC's long-form test: 2–3 personal-story copy variations from a persona/avatar page (e.g., a "waterproof girl" diary) before scaling variation count.

hook: "Hiring: Meta native ad + long-form copy specialist for our health brand." — job-post framing.
body: Hiring a specialist to create native image ads and write long-form ad copy weekly, developing new concepts and iterations based on results; flat fee + commission based on winners (post truncated).
idea: Long-form copy + native image ads are a specialized, commissioned role — brands pay performance-based comp for this skill, which signals the format's ROI.
sequencing: The role (native ad + long-form copy specialist)
The tasks (weekly native images + long copy, iterate on results)
The comp (flat fee + commission on winners)
The truncation (post cut off — full role spec unknown)
why_it_works: As format evidence, a paid hiring post is revealed preference — a health brand paying commission on long-form winners says more about the format's ROI than any guru thread.
what_to_steal: The comp model if LC hires for this: flat fee + commission on winning long-form copy — align the writer with winners, not volume.

hook: "There are 37 ad formats printing right now." — authority list promise.
body: 10 of 37 verified formats; longest runner was an AI podcast at 280 days; full doc linked with live ad + days active + brand ad count per format.
cta: Doc links ("No comment or follow needed").
idea: Format-list proof infrastructure — no VSL-specific content beyond the list's existence.
why_it_works: The days-active proof column, as established in prior folders.
what_to_steal: Nothing VSL-specific — duplicate reference; the folder's real VSL evidence is the two FedotOff90 VSL posts above.
